rejected_revision.prompt:
Use case: style-transfer.
Task: redraw image 1, the EVA engineering SCV concept, with a major reduction in rendering and geometry complexity so it fits the RimWorld game assets in images 2 and 3. Return one isolated transparent sprite only.
Input roles: image 1 is the edit target and broad silhouette/functional idea reference. Image 2 is the authoritative flat game-art reference sheet: study its lower-row safety battery and temperature plugin for thin outlines, flat fill, narrow edge shading, very sparse panel division. Image 3 is the original RimWorld vacuum suit, use only as reference for extremely low visual information at pawn scale; do not copy it or include it.
Keep the SCV-inspired broad shoulders, central glazed single pilot compartment, compact backpack, left cargo claw and right cutter/welder, and yellow/gray industrial palette. Make it compact, stubby and friendly to a one-tile footprint.
Redraw as genuinely simple hand-drawn 2D sprite. Each shoulder is ONE flat muted yellow plate with a single narrow dark edge. Torso is ONE simple light-gray shape surrounding ONE dark blue-green flat window, with only ONE thin window border. Backpack is ONE plain rectangle with two small dark nozzle notches. Each arm has ONE short dark connector and ONE simple tool silhouette. Left claw is a plain U shape, right tool is a plain rectangular head with ONE orange slot. Remove layered elbow cylinders, shoulder bevel facets, knee pads, toe pieces, collar rings, nested chest plating, protruding blue lamps and tiny attachments. Suggest tucked lower body as one simple dark shape.
CRITICAL STYLE: mostly solid flat color, just one small shadow plane per component if needed. Medium thin near-black contour like reference sheet, not the huge black seams in image 1. No gradients, no shine or reflective streak on glass, no soft shading, no texture/noise, no thick faceted bevels, no photorealism, no 3D-render treatment, no highlights on every edge. The image must feel like simple RimWorld art, legible at 48px. Geometric clarity is more important than realism.
Composition: one unit only on transparent square canvas, complete uncropped with generous margin. Overhead orthographic view for a top-down game, nose and tools toward bottom of image (south); keep canopy and shoulder top surfaces visible, avoid front-on humanoid portrait or isometric perspective. No floor, background, shadow, exhaust, beams, text, labels or comparison panels.

review: Restores articulated tool arms, panel seams and nozzle housings. Thinner outlines than first version. Some broad bevel shading remains; overhead angle, four directions and actual-scale QA are not complete.
